# References {.unnumbered}

- [Stanford CME-106 Probability Cheatsheet](https://stanford.edu/~shervine/teaching/cme-106/cheatsheet-probability)

## Core Probability & Mathematical Foundations
- **[18.05 – Introduction to Probability and Statistics (Spring 2022)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-05-introduction-to-probability-and-statistics-spring-2022/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate  
  **Category:** Core probability & statistics  
  **Notes:** Introductory single-semester course combining probability and applied statistics. Core topics: discrete & continuous random variables, expectation, variance, conditional probability and Bayes' rule, sampling distributions, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, simple linear regression, and simulation examples (Monte Carlo).

- **[RES.6-012 – Introduction to Probability (Spring 2018)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate (EECS)  
  **Category:** Core probability (EECS-focused)  
  **Notes:** Independent-study-friendly course emphasizing modeling and problem solving: sample spaces, random variables, distributions, expectation, moment generating functions, limiting distributions, simple random processes. Good bridge between applied engineering problems and mathematical formalism.

- **[6.041 – Probabilistic Systems Analysis and Applied Probability (Fall 2010)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-041-probabilistic-systems-analysis-and-applied-probability-fall-2010/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate  
  **Category:** Applied probability for engineers / EECS  
  **Notes:** Practical modelling of random phenomena: discrete/continuous RVs, conditional probability, Poisson and renewal processes, birth–death processes, basic queueing, transform methods, and elementary inference — frequent in EE/CS curricula.

- **[6.041SC – Probabilistic Systems Analysis and Applied Probability (OCW Scholar, Fall 2013)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-041sc-probabilistic-systems-analysis-and-applied-probability-fall-2013/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate (Self-study)  
  **Category:** Applied probability (OCW Scholar format)  
  **Notes:** Same core content as 6.041 but packaged for independent learners: lecture videos, detailed recitations, problem sets with solutions — excellent for structured self-study.

- **[18.440 – Probability and Random Variables (Spring 2014)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-440-probability-and-random-variables-spring-2014/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate  
  **Category:** Mathematical probability  
  **Notes:** Standard math department probability course: distribution theory (discrete & continuous), joint distributions, conditional distributions, laws of large numbers, central limit theorem, characteristic functions and basic limit results.

- **[18.600 – Probability and Random Variables (Fall 2019)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-600-probability-and-random-variables-fall-2019/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate  
  **Category:** Mathematical probability (updated)  
  **Notes:** Modernized successor to 18.440, covering rigorous treatment of RVs, convergence modes, LLN/CLT, commonly used distributions, and examples geared toward math majors and theoretical foundations.

---

## Advanced Probability Theory
- **[18.175 – Theory of Probability (Spring 2014)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-175-theory-of-probability-spring-2014/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Measure-theoretic probability / theory  
  **Notes:** Rigorous graduate-level course: measure-theoretic foundations, martingales, Brownian motion, Lévy processes, infinite divisibility, advanced limit theorems. Suitable for deep theoretical study and research preparation.

- **[6.436J – Fundamentals of Probability (Fall 2018)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-436j-fundamentals-of-probability-fall-2018/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate (joint EECS/other)  
  **Category:** Rigorous probability for applied disciplines  
  **Notes:** Focus on transforms, multivariate distributions, Poisson processes, Markov chains, generating functions, and limit theorems—designed for students in info theory, communications, and applied probability.

- **[18.226 – Probabilistic Methods in Combinatorics (Fall 2022)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-226-probabilistic-methods-in-combinatorics-fall-2022/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Probabilistic combinatorics / concentration methods  
  **Notes:** Probabilistic tools for discrete math: first & second moment methods, concentration inequalities (Azuma, Chernoff), Lovász Local Lemma, random graphs, threshold phenomena and combinatorial constructions via probabilistic arguments.

---

## Stochastic Processes & Random Systems
- **[18.445 – Introduction to Stochastic Processes (Spring 2015)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-445-introduction-to-stochastic-processes-spring-2015/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Stochastic processes (continuous & discrete)  
  **Notes:** Core stochastic process topics: Markov chains (discrete/continuous), Poisson process, renewal theory, branching processes, martingales, limiting behaviour. Includes examples from physics and biology.

- **[6.262 – Discrete Stochastic Processes (Spring 2011)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-262-discrete-stochastic-processes-spring-2011/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Discrete-time stochastic processes  
  **Notes:** Emphasis on discrete-time models: Markov chains, hitting times, random walks, queuing models, large deviations, and applications. Uses classic texts (Gallager notes included).

- **[15.070J – Advanced Stochastic Processes (Fall 2013)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-070j-advanced-stochastic-processes-fall-2013/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Advanced stochastic theory (OR & finance)  
  **Notes:** Measure-theoretic approach to stochastic processes: stopping times, martingales, Brownian motion, functional limit theorems, elements of Itô calculus and large deviations — applications to finance and operations research.

- **[6.432 – Stochastic Processes, Detection, and Estimation (Spring 2004)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-432-stochastic-processes-detection-and-estimation-spring-2004/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Detection & estimation for stochastic signals  
  **Notes:** Combines stochastic process theory with detection/estimation: hypothesis testing, Neyman–Pearson, Cramér–Rao bounds, Wiener & Kalman filters, spectral representations.

- **[6.231 – Dynamic Programming and Stochastic Control (Fall 2015)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-231-dynamic-programming-and-stochastic-control-fall-2015/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Stochastic control / decision processes  
  **Notes:** Markov decision processes (MDPs), dynamic programming principles, finite/infinite horizon control, partially observable MDPs (POMDPs) and approximation techniques—core for reinforcement learning foundations.

- **[15.072J – Queues: Theory and Applications (Spring 2006)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-072j-queues-theory-and-applications-spring-2006/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Queueing theory & stochastic networks  
  **Notes:** M/M/1, M/G/1, multi-server systems, Little's Law, priority queues, networked queues, heavy traffic limits and performance modelling for service systems.

---

## Probability in Engineering, Uncertainty & Applied Modeling
- **[1.151 – Probability and Statistics in Engineering (Spring 2005)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/1-151-probability-and-statistics-in-engineering-spring-2005/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Engineering-focused probability & stats  
  **Notes:** Bayesian and frequentist inference tailored to engineering problems, parameter estimation, regression, Poisson and renewal processes, reliability and risk assessment techniques.

- **[1.010 – Uncertainty in Engineering (Fall 2008)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/1-010-uncertainty-in-engineering-fall-2008/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate  
  **Category:** Engineering uncertainty & risk modelling  
  **Notes:** Practical exposure to modelling uncertain phenomena in engineering: probability models, propagation of uncertainty, simple reliability models and case studies in civil and environmental engineering.

- **[12.S990 – Quantifying Uncertainty (Fall 2012)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/12-s990-quantifying-uncertainty-fall-2012/)**  
  **Level:** Undergrad/Graduate (Mixed)  
  **Category:** Uncertainty quantification & environmental applications  
  **Notes:** Focus on quantifying uncertainty in Earth sciences and engineering: Monte Carlo simulation, model error, parameter uncertainty, statistical inference and propagation of uncertainty through models.

- **[2.161 – Signal Processing: Continuous and Discrete (Fall 2008)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/2-161-signal-processing-continuous-and-discrete-fall-2008/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate  
  **Category:** Signal processing & stochastic signals  
  **Notes:** Treatment of random signals and noise, correlation functions, spectral analysis, stochastic characterization of signals and filters.

- **[6.011 – Introduction to Communication, Control, and Signal Processing (Spring 2010)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-011-introduction-to-communication-control-and-signal-processing-spring-2010/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate  
  **Category:** Signals & inference foundations  
  **Notes:** Introduces random signals, estimation basics, correlation, detection principles used across communications and control.

- **[HST.582J – Biomedical Signal and Image Processing (Spring 2007)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/hst-582j-biomedical-signal-and-image-processing-spring-2007/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Biomedical stochastic signals & imaging  
  **Notes:** Noise models in biomedical data, stochastic filtering, statistical feature extraction for physiological signals and medical images.

- **[16.322 – Stochastic Estimation and Control (Fall 2004)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/16-322-stochastic-estimation-and-control-fall-2004/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Aerospace / control & estimation  
  **Notes:** Kalman filtering, stochastic models for control, system identification under noise, practical estimation algorithms for aerospace systems.

## Probability in Machine Learning & AI
- **[6.034 – Artificial Intelligence (Fall 2010)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-034-artificial-intelligence-fall-2010/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate  
  **Category:** AI / probabilistic inference  
  **Notes:** Bayesian networks, probabilistic reasoning, inference algorithms (exact & approximate), hidden Markov models and basic learning algorithms—useful for applied probabilistic AI.

- **[6.0002 – Introduction to Computational Thinking & Data Science (Fall 2016)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-0002-introduction-to-computational-thinking-and-data-science-fall-2016/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate  
  **Category:** Computational statistics & simulation  
  **Notes:** Monte Carlo methods, sampling strategies, stochastic simulations for data science tasks, introduction to probabilistic programming patterns in Python.

- **[18.657 – Mathematics of Machine Learning (Fall 2015)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-657-mathematics-of-machine-learning-fall-2015/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Learning theory & probabilistic bounds  
  **Notes:** Concentration inequalities, VC theory, sample complexity, high-probability guarantees for learning algorithms and generalization performance.

- **[15.097 – Prediction: Machine Learning and Statistics (Spring 2012)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-097-prediction-machine-learning-and-statistics-spring-2012/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Statistical prediction & ML  
  **Notes:** Supervised learning framed probabilistically, model selection, cross-validation, uncertainty quantification in predictions.

- **[6.867 – Machine Learning (Fall 2006)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-867-machine-learning-fall-2006/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** ML algorithms with probabilistic foundations  
  **Notes:** Probabilistic models for learning (mixture models, EM), Bayesian approaches, generalization, optimization for probabilistic learners.

- **[18.065 – Matrix Methods in Data Analysis, Signal Processing, and Machine Learning (Spring 2018)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-065-matrix-methods-in-data-analysis-signal-processing-and-machine-learning-spring-2018/)**  
  **Level:** Undergrad/Graduate  
  **Category:** Linear algebra & random matrix applications  
  **Notes:** PCA, SVD, random projections, relationships between matrix methods and stochastic modelling/noise in data.

## Probability in Finance, Economics & Quantitative Modelling
- **[18.S096 – Topics in Mathematics with Applications in Finance (Fall 2013)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-s096-topics-in-mathematics-with-applications-in-finance-fall-2013/)**  
  **Level:** Undergrad/Graduate (Mixed)  
  **Category:** Quantitative finance & stochastic applications  
  **Notes:** Integration of linear algebra, probability, statistics and stochastic processes for finance: risk-neutral pricing concepts, stochastic modelling of asset prices, Monte Carlo methods for pricing and risk.

- **[15.450 – Analytics of Finance (Fall 2010)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-450-analytics-of-finance-fall-2010/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Finance & stochastic calculus  
  **Notes:** Brownian motion, Black–Scholes intuition, Monte Carlo simulation for finance, valuation under uncertainty, portfolio models. Good for quant finance practitioners.

- **[14.01SC – Principles of Microeconomics (Unit: Uncertainty)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/14-01sc-principles-of-microeconomics-fall-2011/pages/unit-6-topics-in-intermediate-microeconomics/uncertainty/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate  
  **Category:** Economics & decision under uncertainty  
  **Notes:** Expected utility theory, risk aversion, insurance, and basic decision theory under uncertainty (module within intro microeconomics).

## Cross-Disciplinary & Applied Courses with Substantial Probability Content
- **[6.042J – Mathematics for Computer Science (Fall 2010)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-042j-mathematics-for-computer-science-fall-2010/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate  
  **Category:** Discrete probability for CS  
  **Notes:** Counting, combinatorics and a focused discrete-probability section: conditional probability, expectation, linearity, random walks and basic probabilistic proofs — essential for algorithmic thinking and randomized algorithms.

- **[6.1200J – Mathematics for Computer Science (Spring 2024)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-1200j-mathematics-for-computer-science-spring-2024/)**  
  **Level:** Undergraduate  
  **Category:** Updated discrete probability for CS  
  **Notes:** Contemporary CS-focused discrete math including discrete probability fundamentals relevant for algorithms, complexity, and probabilistic analysis.

- **[8.591J / 7.81J / 7.32 – Systems Biology (Fall 2014)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/8-591j-systems-biology-fall-2014/)**  
  **Level:** Mixed Undergrad/Graduate  
  **Category:** Biological stochastic modelling  
  **Notes:** Stochastic models in biology: stochastic gene expression, noise in biochemical networks, probabilistic simulation of cellular systems.

- **[HST.582J / 6.555J / 16.456 – Biomedical Signal & Image Processing (Spring 2007)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/hst-582j-biomedical-signal-and-image-processing-spring-2007/)**  
  **Level:** Graduate  
  **Category:** Biomedical data & stochastic methods  
  **Notes:** Application of stochastic signal processing methods to biomedical imaging and signals; estimation under noise and statistical feature extraction.

- **[12.S990 – Quantifying Uncertainty (Fall 2012)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/12-s990-quantifying-uncertainty-fall-2012/)**  
  **Level:** Undergrad/Graduate (Mixed)  
  **Category:** Interdisciplinary uncertainty quantification  
  **Notes:** Cross-disciplinary practical methods for quantifying uncertainty in environmental models and geoscience contexts—Monte Carlo, Bayesian updates, and model/data uncertainty.
